actions.name: Camera inspection of hands and wrists
actions.result: Symmetric soft-tissue swelling over the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints and both wrist joints bilaterally, with mild overlying erythema. No visible nodules, no skin rash, no digital ulcers. Fingers are not deviated.

actions.name: Patient-guided squeeze test (MCP/MTP compression)
actions.result: Patient reports pain on self-compression across the MCP joints of both hands and across the forefoot (MTP squeeze), consistent with synovitis.

actions.name: Patient-guided grip strength / fist closure
actions.result: Patient can make a full fist bilaterally but reports pain doing so, worse on the right; no fixed contracture seen on camera.

actions.name: Camera inspection of feet (forefoot/MTP region)
actions.result: Mild swelling across the forefoot bilaterally at the metatarsal heads, tender to patient self-palpation. No ulcers, no rash.

actions.name: Skin and nail inspection via camera (psoriasis screen)
actions.result: No psoriatic plaques, no nail pitting, onycholysis, or oil-drop changes seen on camera.

actions.name: Review home vitals (temperature, weight)
actions.result: Temperature 98.2°F (36.8°C), weight stable, no fevers reported.

actions.name: Review anti-CCP antibody
actions.result: Anti-CCP >250 U/mL (H) — reference <20 U/mL, strongly positive.

actions.name: Review inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR)
actions.result: CRP 22 mg/L (H, reference <5 mg/L); ESR 41 mm/h (H, reference <20 mm/h).

actions.name: Review CBC and liver enzymes
actions.result: CBC within normal limits; AST/ALT within normal limits.

actions.name: Review hepatitis B serology
actions.result: Hepatitis B surface antigen negative; hepatitis B core antibody positive, consistent with prior resolved infection — relevant before starting biologic/targeted immunosuppression (reactivation risk).

actions.name: Review hand/wrist X-ray report
actions.result: Bilateral periarticular osteopenia at MCP joints; no erosions identified; joint spaces preserved.

actions.name: Review medication list
actions.result: Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for joint pain; prenatal vitamin; no DMARDs on file.

actions.name: Tender/swollen joint count (28-joint assessment)
actions.result: Tender joint count 10 and swollen joint count 8 across bilateral MCPs, wrists, and MTPs. Combined with CRP 22 mg/L (once reviewed) and patient global assessment, this joint count pattern is consistent with moderate-to-high disease activity; a formal DAS28-CRP score can be calculated once CRP and patient global assessment (0-10) are incorporated.

actions.name: Review home morning stiffness/pain diary
actions.result: Patient-logged diary shows morning stiffness averaging 85-100 minutes daily over the past 2 weeks, pain 6/10 on most mornings improving to 3/10 by midday.

cells: As needed, up to 3x/day for joint pain

artifacts.title: X-ray Bilateral Hands and Wrists
artifacts.author: Radiology - Seattle Imaging Associates
artifacts.body:
FINDINGS: Bilateral periarticular osteopenia involving the 2nd-4th MCP joints and carpal rows. Joint spaces are preserved. No marginal erosions identified. No chondrocalcinosis. No significant degenerative changes.
IMPRESSION: Periarticular osteopenia without erosive change, which may be an early finding in inflammatory arthritis. Recommend clinical correlation and follow-up imaging if diagnosis of inflammatory arthropathy confirmed.

objectives.text: Elicit a history consistent with inflammatory (vs mechanical) polyarthritis, including symmetric small joint involvement, prolonged morning stiffness, and gradual progression.
Recognize family history and serologic pattern (RF, anti-CCP, inflammatory markers) supporting a diagnosis of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, and correlate with imaging.

Screen for and interpret pre-treatment safety labs, including hepatitis B serology, recognizing the implications of isolated core antibody positivity before starting immunosuppressive/biologic therapy.

Elicit reproductive health history (pregnancy intention) and herbal/complementary medication use through direct interview (not the written medication list, which does not capture undisclosed supplement use), and recognize how these change treatment planning (avoiding methotrexate; need to clarify unidentified herbal supplement).
Perform a systematic review of systems to exclude alternative diagnoses (psoriatic arthritis, lupus, gout) using pertinent negatives.

Formulate a management plan within rheumatology scope: confirm diagnosis of early seropositive RA, discuss conventional DMARD options compatible with conception plans, address herbal supplement safety, and coordinate hepatitis B monitoring/specialist input as needed.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Early seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (symmetric small-joint polyarthritis, RF and anti-CCP strongly positive, elevated CRP/ESR, periarticular osteopenia without erosions, family history of RA)
differential: Psoriatic arthritis (less likely: no psoriasis, nail changes, or dactylitis; distal/asymmetric pattern not present)
Systemic lupus erythematosus (less likely: no malar rash, oral ulcers, photosensitivity, or serositis reported)
Gout/crystal arthropathy (less likely: not monoarticular/episodic, no classic podagra pattern, chronic symmetric course)
Osteoarthritis (unlikely given inflammatory features: prolonged morning stiffness >60 min, symmetric swelling, elevated inflammatory markers)
keyFindings: 3 months of symmetric MCP and wrist swelling/pain, now with forefoot (MTP) involvement
Morning stiffness ~90 minutes, improving but not fully resolving by afternoon
Family history of RF-positive RA with deformities in mother
RF 84 IU/mL and anti-CCP >250 U/mL, both strongly positive
CRP 22 mg/L and ESR 41 mm/h elevated
Hand/wrist X-ray showing periarticular osteopenia without erosions (early disease)
Hepatitis B core antibody positive with negative surface antigen (prior exposure, reactivation risk with future biologic/targeted therapy)
Patient actively trying to conceive, which precludes methotrexate and some other teratogenic DMARDs
Unidentified herbal supplement use that needs safety review before starting new prescription therapy
plan: Confirm diagnosis of early seropositive RA using 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria (joint distribution, serology, acute phase reactants, duration)

Counsel that methotrexate and other teratogenic agents (e.g., leflunomide) are contraindicated given active attempts to conceive; discuss conception-compatible options such as hydroxychloroquine and/or sulfasalazine, and judicious short-term low-dose corticosteroid bridging if needed, in conjunction with discussion of family planning timeline
Advise discontinuing the unidentified herbal preparation until ingredients can be identified, given unknown interactions and lack of labeling; document discussion

Order baseline safety labs/arrange monitoring plan consistent with chosen therapy; given hepatitis B core antibody positivity with negative surface antigen, flag reactivation risk and plan hepatitis B DNA/viral load check and consider gastroenterology/hepatology or infectious disease input before any future biologic or targeted synthetic DMARD, even though not needed for hydroxychloroquine/sulfasalazine specifically
Reinforce NSAID use for symptom control and address inconsistent dosing/stomach concerns; discuss safer dosing strategy or alternative symptom control if GI concerns persist
Refer/coordinate with obstetrics or maternal-fetal medicine given active pregnancy planning and need for coordinated rheumatic disease management through conception and pregnancy
Schedule close follow-up (4-6 weeks) to reassess joint counts, inflammatory markers, and treatment tolerance; monitor for any new erosive change on future imaging if clinically indicated
Patient education on the chronic, treatable nature of RA, the goal of early treatment to prevent joint damage, and realistic expectations given her mother's disease course
redFlags: Strongly positive anti-CCP (>250 U/mL) and elevated inflammatory markers indicating higher risk for erosive, deforming disease without timely treatment
Active desire to conceive restricting standard first-line DMARD (methotrexate) and requiring careful medication selection
Hepatitis B core antibody positivity requiring attention before any future immunosuppressive escalation to avoid viral reactivation
Unknown/unregulated herbal supplement with unclear contents, which could mask symptoms, interact with future therapy, or itself cause harm
educationPoints: Early seropositive RA (positive RF/anti-CCP, elevated acute phase reactants) carries higher risk of erosive joint damage and benefits from prompt DMARD initiation to prevent long-term deformity.

Family planning intentions must be addressed before DMARD selection, since methotrexate and leflunomide are teratogenic and other options (hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine) are preferred during conception attempts and pregnancy.

Isolated hepatitis B core antibody positivity (surface antigen negative) indicates past exposure and carries a risk of reactivation with future biologic or targeted synthetic DMARD therapy, warranting viral load monitoring and specialist consultation if escalation is needed.

Patients may use herbal or traditional remedies from family members; routine, nonjudgmental screening for these is essential since ingredients are often unknown and could affect safety or efficacy of prescribed therapy.

Periarticular osteopenia without erosions on early imaging does not exclude a diagnosis of RA; absence of erosions is expected early in disease and should not delay treatment when clinical and serologic criteria are met.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient reports taking ibuprofen only when pain is bad and sometimes skipping doses due to stomach concerns, suggesting inconsistent, lower-than-prescribed use
mismatches.recordEvidence: Medication list documents ibuprofen 400 mg as needed up to 3 times daily, suggesting the regimen on record is already flexible/PRN rather than a fixed schedule she is under-taking - the mismatch is that despite feeling she is 'under-using' it, the record shows no fixed dosing was ever prescribed, so her guilt about 'skipping doses' reflects a misunderstanding of her own regimen rather than true nonadherence
mismatches.teachingPoint: Clarify the actual prescribed regimen versus patient perception; patients may feel they are 'not taking medication as directed' when the regimen was already PRN, highlighting the importance of reviewing the medication list with the patient to correct misunderstandings and address underlying concerns (e.g., GI side effects) directly.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient states she is unsure of her hepatitis B vaccination status and has no known history of hepatitis illness, implying she may be unexposed or only vaccine-protected
mismatches.recordEvidence: Lab report shows hepatitis B core antibody positive with surface antigen negative and surface antibody negative, indicating prior natural infection (not vaccination, since surface antibody alone would be expected from vaccination) that has since resolved, which the patient was unaware of
mismatches.teachingPoint: A positive core antibody with negative surface antibody indicates past natural hepatitis B infection rather than vaccine-induced immunity; patients often cannot report this distinction themselves, so interpreting serology correctly (rather than relying on patient-reported vaccine/infection history) is essential before immunosuppressive therapy planning.

scenario.studentBrief: You are a rheumatology fellow conducting a new telehealth consultation. Mei-Ling Chow, 41, was referred by her primary care physician for 3 months of hand and wrist pain and swelling, now also involving her feet. Baseline labs and hand X-rays were obtained prior to the visit and are available in the chart. Conduct a focused history and guided remote examination, review the available labs and imaging, and develop an assessment and plan.

profile.summary: A 41-year-old pastry chef with 3 months of symmetric hand/wrist swelling and morning stiffness, now with forefoot involvement, strongly positive RF and anti-CCP, elevated inflammatory markers, and non-erosive periarticular osteopenia consistent with early seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. The case teaches history-taking for inflammatory arthritis, interpretation of safety labs (notably hepatitis B core antibody positivity), and treatment planning complicated by active pregnancy intention and undisclosed herbal supplement use.
